notes:
Account summary: Helix builds an enterprise-scale retrieval layer for major European financial & legal customers. Focus: massive-scale embeddings (200M-1B vectors) + reranking pipeline. Needs: sub-150ms p95 end-to-end for interactive search, steady-state throughput 200-500 QPS across EU/NA, and unit cost pressure — target <$0.0015/query at scale.

POC specifics: Helix delivered 600M vectors (S3) for initial perf run. Current architecture: custom quantized embeddings (PQ + product quantization), HNSW index for candidate retrieval, then cross-encoder reranker for top-50. Problem areas called out: reranker cost dominates, cold-start latency on some shards, and distributed nearest-neighbor memory footprint. Helix is heavy on cost engineering — want batching, KV/prefix caching, and dynamic rerank thresholds (only rerank top-N when signal warrants).

Security/compliance: Must support SSO/SAML, EU data residency, KMS-based key mgmt and audit logs. Asked about Private deployment (on prem or VPC) for regulated customers. Quote from CTO: "We can accept small accuracy delta if it halves our per-query cost — economics rule here."

Sales notes: AE demoed Redwood batching and cache proposals; SE did a deep-dive on reranking fallbacks. Procurement is sensitive to long-term committed spend but wants predictable unit economics. Internal stakeholders: CTO (search infra), Head of Ops (cost), Security Lead (compliance).

technical_requirements: Index scale target: initially 200M-600M vectors, roadmap to 1B+ within 12–18 months
Throughput target: 200–500 QPS sustained, burst to 1k QPS
Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end target <150ms for standard searches; p99 <350ms optional
Reranking pattern: cross-encoder on top-K (K=20–50) with ability to selectively skip rerank based on recency/signal
Cost target: <$0.0015 per query at production scale (including retrieval + rerank)
Storage constraints: prefer quantized indexes (IVF/PQ) to reduce memory footprint and egress costs
Routing needs: EU-first routing, failover to NA but never store EU PII outside EU without consent
integration_notes: Helix uses a mix of FAISS-based offline pipelines and a custom online HNSW cluster. They want Redwood to integrate as the serving layer (ANN + rerank orchestration) and to keep FAISS as the offline builder. Interested in Redwood-managed index shards for Dedicated with S3-backed shard recovery. Also evaluating hybrid retrieval (sparse BM25 warmup + dense ANN).
poc_metrics_summary: Baseline (Helix infra): ANN retrieval 60ms avg, cross-encoder rerank adds 260ms; end-to-end p95 ~320ms. After Redwood batching/proposal (simulated): expected rerank reduction to ~90–120ms when using dynamic top-K and batching; cost reduction estimate 40–60% on rerank stage. SE note: simulations assume 8–16 token cross-encoder or distilled reranker variants.
objections_and_risks: Primary objection is budget and storage economics for 1B vectors. Risk: reranker accuracy loss if using distillation/quantization; Helix legal requires strict EU residency terms that push towards Private deployment. Ops team concerned about complexity of shard recovery across Dedicated nodes.
